title: Cells as the Basic Units of Life
summary: Cell structure and the functions of organelles, plant and animal cells compared, using a microscope, and how cells form tissues, organs and systems.

notes.text: All living things are made of **cells**, the smallest units that can carry out the processes of life. Some organisms, such as bacteria and amoebas, are **unicellular** (one cell). Plants and animals are **multicellular**, made of millions of specialised cells.

notes.caption: Parts of a cell and their functions
rows: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
Jelly-like fluid where chemical reactions take place
Controls the cell's activities; contains genetic material (DNA)
Made of cellulose; gives shape, support and protection
Stores water and dissolved substances; keeps the cell firm

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Three structures are found ONLY in plant cells: the **cell wall**, **chloroplasts** and a **large central vacuole**. Plant cells are usually rectangular; animal cells are usually rounded or irregular.

notes.text:
In multicellular organisms, cells are organised in levels:

**cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism**

rows: A group of similar cells that perform the same function
Organs working together for one major function

notes.text: Cells are **specialised** for their jobs: red blood cells have no nucleus and a dimpled disc shape to carry more oxygen; nerve cells are long to carry messages; root hair cells have a long extension to absorb water; guard cells open and close stomata.

notes.title: Putting the levels in order
notes.problem: Arrange these from smallest to largest: heart, muscle cell, human, circulatory system, muscle tissue.
steps: Start with one cell: muscle cell.
Similar cells working together make a tissue: muscle tissue.
Different tissues form an organ: heart.
Organs working together form a system: circulatory system. All the systems make the organism: human.
notes.answer: Muscle cell → muscle tissue → heart → circulatory system → human.

questions.prompt: Explain how a red blood cell is adapted to its function.

✓ Function: carries oxygen (1)
✓ Adaptation: no nucleus / biconcave disc shape gives more space and a large surface area for oxygen (1)
